| 6 | Custom solid silicone noise plugs | A | B* | Individually fitted attenuation; water use requires explicit manufacturer approval. |
| 7 | Reusable flanged silicone plugs | A* | A* | Seal by flexible flanges rather than adhesion. Correct size and insertion matter. |
| 8 | Flanged thermoplastic elastomer plugs | A* | A* | Beeswax-free alternative to silicone; formulation and skin tolerance vary. |
| 9 | Commercial moldable synthetic-wax plugs explicitly labelled beeswax-free | A* | A* | Potentially the closest functional alternative to beeswax plugs. Check the full ingredients; “wax” alone does not mean beeswax-free. |

| 18 | Disposable polyurethane foam plugs | A | B | Inexpensive, established noise protection when correctly fitted. Generally a poor choice for repeated swimming use. |
| 19 | Filtered musician’s earplugs | A* | X* | Reduce sound while better preserving its balance; choose sufficient attenuation for the actual exposure. |
| 20 | Protective earmuffs | A | X | Avoid canal contact and adhesive ingredients. Often the simplest option for sensitive ear canals. |
